attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, asserting this himself.

semantics.note: 'That clearly isn't the case' is a firm factual assertion that Apple did not train only on licensed content. The conditional about Google/DeviantArt and the pillaging language are rightly treated as separate.

contract.note: The contract keeps how content was obtained separate from whether it was licensed, and counts open licenses as licenses. That is a careful but ordinary reading. The result turns on whether Apple's split between 'licensed data' and crawled public data shows that some content was unlicensed, and the contract says crawler collection alone does not show that.

evidence.note: Apple's own disclosure (2024-06-10) lists licensed data and, separately, public data gathered by AppleBot, with an opt-out. It implies not everything was negotiated, but it does not show that any included item lacked an applicable license.

reviews.rationale: The only evidence is Apple's disclosure. It says crawled public web data was used alongside licensed data, but under the contract that does not establish unlicensed use. No record shows that a specific training item was unlicensed, and no complete rights inventory shows that everything was licensed. The packet supports neither condition, so the claim is unresolved.
